slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and how should it be packaged and priced to lift NRR from 101% to 105% by 2028 with gross margin at or above 75%?
How much expansion revenue can Copilot add, and which package gets it?
Will Copilot keep customers and win deals against Routewise?
Can Copilot run inside the 75% margin floor and pay back its build?
Is Copilot worth delaying the mobile rewrite by two quarters?
How should we launch it, and how will we know it is working?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO and executive team, at January 2027 planning
NRR rises from 101% to 105% by 2028; Company gross margin stays at or above 75%; The mobile app rewrite slips no more than two quarters
January 2027 planning
Changes to the Core plan price; Building our own AI model; Scope and design of the mobile app rewrite

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a new Pro tier at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, not as a $149 add-on
A Pro tier would add about $2.9M of ARR and 5 percentage points of NRR; the $8M add-on case rests on a biased survey
–	Asked to pay $149, 14% of beta accounts bought, not the 46% surveyed
Copilot's retention and win-back gains are real but too small to justify the launch alone
–	Only 6% of churned accounts left for AI features
Copilot keeps margin above 75% and pays back in about 1.6 years, with usage pooled under about 505 requests a seat
–	Inference costs about $4 a seat a month, a third of Pro's $12
The mobile delay risks at most $1.1M of ARR; waiting wins only if the rewrite would end over half of mobile churn
–	A perfect mobile fix adds at most 3.8 percentage points of NRR
Launch Pro by the end of June 2027, return the 14 engineers to mobile in July, and steer by five gates
–	Under 13% of accounts on Pro after six months triggers a re-price
